notes: Cognitive walkthrough (full four-question variant) of the critical journey reserve-tool-for-saturday at 375 px, light theme. The record is at cw/reserve-tool-for-saturday.json. Evidence refs are relative to the run directory. All candidates are E0 hypotheses. The journey file's _comment mentions a ground-truth file; I did not open it.

task_suitability.evidence: probes/33/final.png ('Reservation confirmed', Saturday 17 October, two-battery drill)

candidates.title: 'Reserve this tool' only adds to the basket, and nothing says the reservation is unfinished
candidates.description: CW-Q4 fails at step 6 and CW-Q1 at step 7. The tool page's main button says 'Reserve this tool'. Tapping it shows only a small toast, 'Added to your basket', which has gone within 6 s; the button and the visible page do not change. A first-time member, who does not know how the basket works, has pressed 'Reserve' and has no cue that a session and their details are still needed. They may leave believing the drill is reserved. Missing feedback: that the tool is only held. Missing knowledge: that the basket must be checked out.
candidates.impact: A member may believe the drill is reserved when it is not, and arrive at Saturday's session to find no reservation.

evidence.detail: after Reserve: toast 'Added to your basket' over the calendar; button label unchanged; header count off screen
6 s after Reserve the toast is gone and the screen looks as before the tap
status: Added to your basket; button 'Reserve this tool'

factor_notes.impact: step 7 verdict would_not: the persona may stop here thinking the task is done
factor_notes.persistence: first-time and infrequent members (a handful of times a year) meet it each time they forget the flow

candidates.recommendation: Say what happened and what is next, e.g. 'Held in your basket – choose a session to finish reserving', with a link to the basket; or name the button for what it does.

candidates.title: No visible way on to the basket after adding a tool on a phone
candidates.description: CW-Q2 fails at step 7. After 'Reserve this tool', the page stays scrolled to the calendar. The only route on, the 'Basket (1)' text link in the header, is out of view. The toast has no link and disappears. There is no next-step button on the tool page. Missing knowledge: where to go to finish.
candidates.impact: Members who do realise more is needed have to scroll up and recognise the header count as the way forward.

evidence.detail: viewport after Reserve: no header, no basket link, toast without a link
after 6 s: toast gone, no way on visible

candidates.recommendation: Offer a visible 'Go to basket' / 'Choose a session' action in the toast or in place of the Reserve button once added.

candidates.title: The two cordless drills' titles are cut to the same text on a phone
candidates.description: CW-Q3 fails at step 4. At 375 px both search results read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…', with the same category, deposit and availability. The part that tells them apart, 'two batteries' or 'one battery', is cut off. The member is looking for 'the drill with two batteries' and cannot tell which card to open. Missing knowledge: which card is the two-battery drill.
candidates.impact: The member may open the one-battery drill, or must open both cards to compare.

locations.selector: role=link[name="Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries"]
role=link[name="Cordless drill 18 V, combi, one battery"]

evidence.detail: both result titles shown as 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…'
full names differ only in 'two batteries' / 'one battery'

candidates.recommendation: Let tool titles wrap instead of truncating, or surface the distinguishing detail (battery count) on the card.

candidates.title: On a phone the pick-up calendar is below the fold, under a sticky Reserve button
candidates.description: CW-Q2 fails at step 5. The first screen of the tool page ends at the 'Pick-up day' heading, with the sticky 'Reserve this tool' button over it; the calendar and its instructions are out of view. The most visible action is Reserve. Tapping it first gives 'Choose a pick-up day first.', so the member recovers, but only after an error. Missing knowledge: that a day must be chosen below before reserving.
candidates.impact: First-time members meet an error before they find the day picker.

evidence.detail: first screen: sticky Reserve button over the 'Pick-up day' heading; no calendar visible
Reserve without a day: red 'Choose a pick-up day first.' above the calendar

candidates.recommendation: Signal the required choice before the button (e.g. disabled-looking state with 'Choose a pick-up day' text, or place the picker before details on small screens).

candidates.title: The basket asks for a pick-up session again, with nothing preselected, after a pick-up day was chosen
candidates.description: CW-Q1 fails at step 8. On the tool page the member chose Saturday 17 October as the pick-up day, and the basket card repeats 'Pick up Saturday 17 October'. The basket then asks for a 'Pick-up session' with no option selected. A member who thinks this is already done may tap Continue and get 'There is a problem: Choose a pick-up session'. Missing knowledge: that pick-up day and pick-up session are separate choices.
candidates.impact: An extra, apparently repeated decision; risk of an error and of choosing a session that differs from the pick-up day.

evidence.detail: card says 'Pick up Saturday 17 October'; no session radio is selected
Continue without a session: 'There is a problem – Choose a pick-up session'

candidates.recommendation: Preselect the session matching the chosen pick-up day, or explain why a session is chosen separately.

candidates.title: Pick-up sessions are listed latest first, the reverse of the calendar
candidates.description: CW-Q3 fails at step 8. On screen the sessions run Wed 28, Sat 24, Wed 21, Sat 17, Wed 14, Sat 10 October, while the calendar on the previous page ran forwards. A member scanning down for 'Saturday' meets 'Saturday 24 October' first and may choose it. The accessibility tree lists the radios earliest first, so screen-reader and visual orders also differ. Missing knowledge: that the list is in reverse date order.
candidates.impact: A member may reserve for the wrong Saturday.

evidence.detail: visual order Wed 28 first, Sat 10 last
radios in DOM order Sat 10 … Wed 28

candidates.recommendation: List sessions in date order, matching the calendar and the DOM order.

candidates.title: 'Continue' and 'Confirm reservation' give no visible response for over a second
candidates.description: CW-Q4 fails at steps 9 and 11. After tapping 'Continue' nothing on screen changes for about 1.2 s before the confirm page loads. After 'Confirm reservation' nothing changes for about 1.5 s before 'Reservation confirmed'. Neither button shows a pressed or busy state. A member on a phone may think the tap missed and tap again. Missing feedback: immediate acknowledgement of the tap.
candidates.impact: Uncertainty at the final commit step; repeat taps.

evidence.detail: expect /confirm.html after Continue took 1,223 ms; step-05.png right after the tap shows the unchanged basket
expect 'Reservation confirmed' after Confirm took 1,555 ms; step-10.png shows the unchanged form

candidates.recommendation: Show a busy state on the button at once and ignore repeat taps while the request runs.

candidates.title: After confirming, the header still shows 'Basket (1)'
candidates.description: CW-Q4 partly fails at step 11. The 'Reservation confirmed' page is clear, but the header still reads 'Basket (1)'. That suggests something is still pending. A cautious member may open the basket, find the drill still there, and wonder whether the reservation went through or whether a second one would be made. Missing feedback: a basket count that reflects the completed reservation.
candidates.impact: Doubt about whether the reservation is complete; possible repeat reservation.
candidates.recommendation: Empty the basket once the reservation is confirmed.

candidates.title: On a phone, the tool search sits below the whole catalogue
candidates.description: CW-Q2 fails at step 2. At 375 px the 'Search tools' field and 'Search' button come after all 10 tool cards, about 2,100 px down the page. A member wanting a specific tool sees no search in the first screens. Missing knowledge: that search exists and where it is. In this journey the member can still tap the drill from the list, so the effect is extra scrolling.
candidates.impact: Search is effectively hidden on phones; finding a tool means scrolling the list.

evidence.detail: full page: search region after the 10 tool cards

candidates.recommendation: Place search (and filters) above the tool list.
